cards.explanation: The answer is signs. Nicodemus, a Pharisee and a leader of the Jews, says, “For no one could perform the signs You are doing if God were not with him.” He's telling Jesus what he has noticed and what he thinks it means. I think the man had a lot on his mind before he ever came to Jesus.

The answer is his mother's womb. Nicodemus asks, “Can he enter his mother’s womb a second time to be born?” He starts with “How can a man be born when he is old?” I think he's picturing it exactly as Jesus said it, and honestly, that picture makes me want to sit down.

The answer is amazed. Jesus says, “Do not be amazed that I said, ‘You must be born again.’” He says it right after talking about being born of the Spirit. I think a little amazement is understandable, friends.

The answer is that you can hear its sound. Jesus says, “You hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it is going.” The sound shows up even when the rest stays a mystery. It's like hearing the oven timer from the other room and still having no idea who set it.

The answer is True. Jesus says the wind blows where it wishes, then adds, “So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” The wind is His picture for them. Nicodemus had just asked about being born, and this is the picture Jesus gives next.

The answer is Israel's teacher. Jesus says, “You are Israel’s teacher…” and then asks if he does not understand these things. It's a big title to be handed right before a question like that. I'd feel the weight of it for sure.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “…and yet you people do not accept our testimony.” He says that straight after talking about what they have seen. That's the text's own wording, so we leave it just as it is.

The answer is heavenly things. Jesus says, “If I have told you about earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?” He's asking about the next step up. And I'm still working on the earthly ones myself.

The answer is the Son of Man. Jesus says, “Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up…” Moses is the one who lifted the snake. And Son of Man is the name Jesus uses for Himself (Mark 2:10).

The answer is eternal. Jesus says it's “…that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.” Everyone who believes, no list of exceptions attached. That's a big word, friends, and it's the word He uses.

The answer is to save the world through Him. Jesus says, “For God did not send His Son into the world to condemn the world, but to save the world through Him.” First what He didn't come to do, then what He did. Short and clear, my favorite kind of teaching.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…whoever does not believe has already been condemned, because he has not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son.” He says it plainly. This is one of those lines I read slowly.

The answer is that they loved the darkness instead. Jesus says, “The Light has come into the world, but men loved the darkness rather than the Light…” It's a heavy line, and I won't pretend otherwise. Light came, and that's how people answered it.
The answer is deeds. Jesus says men loved the darkness rather than the Light “…because their deeds were evil.” That's the reason He gives. And to be clear, He's the one giving it.

The answer is that he fears his deeds will be exposed. Jesus says, “Everyone who does evil hates the Light, and does not come into the Light for fear that his deeds will be exposed.” The fear is about what the Light would show. I think that's a heavy thing to carry around.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “But whoever practices the truth comes into the Light, so that it may be seen clearly that what he has done has been accomplished in God.” They come toward the Light and don't stay away. I think that's a beautiful verse.
